learning_objective: 🎯 Become a master describer by learning how to compare people, places, and things using amazing adjectives!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Adjectives are wonderful describing words! They add color and details to nouns, telling us how something looks, feels, sounds, or tastes. Like a 'sweet' apple or a 'brave' hero.
When we compare things, adjectives change their form! We use the Positive degree for one thing (tall), Comparative for two things (taller), and Superlative for three or more (tallest).
For big, long adjectives, we do not add '-er' or '-est'. Instead, we use 'more' and 'most'! For example: beautiful, MORE beautiful, MOST beautiful.

fun_activity.title: 📏 The Size Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Find three books of different sizes in your house. Write a sentence comparing them using the words: thick, thicker, and thickest!

quick_recap: ⭐ Adjectives are words that describe nouns and pronouns.
⭐ Add '-er' to compare two things, and '-est' to compare more than two.
⭐ Long words use 'more' and 'most' instead of changing their endings.
